learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of breaking down problems and designing step-by-step solutions using algorithms and flowcharts before writing any code!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Programming is just problem solving. The steps are: 1) Analyze the problem, 2) Develop an Algorithm, 3) Code the solution, and 4) Test and Debug the code.
An algorithm is a finite, step-by-step set of instructions to solve a specific problem. It should be clear, unambiguous, and have a definite starting and ending point.
A flowchart is a visual representation of an algorithm using standardized symbols: Oval (Start/Stop), Parallelogram (Input/Output), Rectangle (Process), and Diamond (Decision).
Pseudocode is an informal way of writing an algorithm using plain English-like statements. It doesn't follow strict programming syntax but outlines the logic perfectly.
Breaking down a large, complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems. It makes solving the overall problem much easier.

fun_activity.title: ☕ The Tea Algorithm
fun_activity.instructions: Write an algorithm (step-by-step instructions) on how to make a cup of tea. Hand it to a friend and ask them to follow it exactly. Did you forget to tell them to turn on the stove? Algorithms require perfect detail!

exam_tips: 📌 Always use the correct shapes for flowcharts (Oval for start/stop, Diamond for decision/if-else).
📌 Remember that an algorithm must always have a finite number of steps (it must eventually stop).
📌 Understand that pseudocode is independent of any specific programming language.
quick_recap: ⭐ Analyzing the problem is the crucial first step before writing any algorithm or code.
⭐ Debugging is the process of identifying and removing errors (bugs) from a program.
⭐ A diamond symbol in a flowchart implies a question with a Yes/No (True/False) answer, controlling the flow.
